decision_risks: Sell before expiry

A failed or slow marketing period as the remaining term shortens; transfer tax of 4.45% or 5.95% if the parcel is in the City of Los Angeles and the price is above the threshold; federal, state and net-investment-income tax on the gain; proceeds reinvested at a lower yield.
Low after closing: the earthquake, wildfire and tenant-failure exposure passes to the buyer. A catastrophe or a credit event during marketing can still remove the bid.
Start early, keep the process confidential, obtain two or three independent price opinions, and compute net proceeds with the owner's real basis before accepting.
ULA
Sell with a §1031 exchange
The same sale risks, plus the risk of overpaying for a replacement to meet the exchange rules; deferral, not elimination, of tax; a new concentration in whatever is bought.
The hazard profile of the replacement replaces that of Asset A. A replacement outside the Los Angeles region removes the correlated earthquake and wildfire exposure; one inside it does not.
Identify and underwrite replacement candidates before closing; use a qualified intermediary; take tax advice first.
IRS1031
Negotiate an early renewal or extension
Concessions to obtain the signature; rent fixed below cost inflation; a weak or absent guaranty; the issuer is closing 50-60 restaurants in FY2026 and reports same-store sales of -1.1%.
Fully retained: one building, one tenant, one region. A regional catastrophe can stop the rent and the exit at the same time.
Obtain the legal obligor and guaranty in writing; compare term, rent, credit and concessions with the sale and hold alternatives; check the 35-year leasehold rule before adding options.
SECQ3
Hold under the existing lease to expiry
The term shortens every year and with it the pool of buyers and lenders; vacancy at expiry removes all rent while taxes, insurance and re-letting costs continue.
Fully retained, for the longest period of any route, and with the least room to react.
Only defensible with a funded re-letting reserve, verified insurance and a dated decision point well before the notice window.
IR25
Renew, then sell
Two sets of costs; no assurance that a longer term raises the bid by more than the concessions cost; a higher interest rate at the later sale date lowers price for the same rent.
Retained until the later sale. The 30-year likelihood of an M6.7 or larger earthquake in the Los Angeles region is 60%.
Compare real bids for the property as it is against indicative bids with the extension before conceding anything.
FRED
Re-tenant or reposition
Downtime with no rent, leasing commissions, tenant improvements, and the possible loss of drive-through rights if the use lapses. No evidence of alternative demand was obtained.
Fully retained, and the building is vacant or in transition when the event happens.
Confirm zoning and entitlements first; obtain a signed letter of intent from a replacement tenant before giving up the current one.
ZIMAS
Redevelop or ground lease
Entitlement, construction, financing and environmental risk; the widest spread of outcomes; years without income.
Fully retained and increased: more capital is committed to one parcel in one hazard region.
Not a wealth-preservation default. Needs a parcel, a feasibility study and an independently costed residual land value.
ZIMAS
Run both tracks in parallel (recommended)
Advisory cost and effort; lease terms that restrict marketing or assignment; the tenant learning of the sale process and hardening its renewal position.
Retained only until one track closes; this route shortens the exposure without forcing a sale.
Confidential process, a written renewal request with a response date, and a pre-agreed rule for choosing between the two results.
